en: In the *Śūra-bhikṣu-sūtra*, Rāma asked: "Furthermore, [there is] a certain method by which one may also escape [this]. Śūra..."
[He] asked about his intention.
The Great Sage replied:

"If one reverently believes in the Three [Jewels], observes the fasts, performs prostrations, and maintains this reverent faith without slackening, focusing single-mindedly [on these practices], then even the calamity of the great waters [cannot harm them]."
Śūra again asked the Great Seer:
"[... the calamity of illness.
The Great Seer said:

"Monks, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās—from this day forward, maintain the precepts and observe the fasts so that they are all pure. Understand and practice what you have learned; you should receive the precepts exactly as I have instructed, and not according to your ordinary ways, for only then can you attain deliverance. Śūra said:
He further asked, "What expedient means can be employed to escape the calamities of malevolent spirits?
The Great Seer replied, "As for these malevolent spirits, there are many kinds that obey my commands; you must be careful not to trust them."
When the Moonlight Tathāgata appears in the world, only those who possess exclusively wholesome qualities are able to see him;
sentient beings who have committed the five heinous crimes will never see him. Śūra asked:
"What are the features of its cities, moats, and streets?
The Great Seer replied: "The cities, moats, and streets are seven hundred li in length and breadth;
they are one thousand feet high and have foundations one thousand feet deep."
The city walls are over five hundred feet high and feature seventy-two gates;
the walls are the color of purple-polished gold.
Within it is the city of Tuṣita,
one thousand cubits high with foundations one thousand cubits deep;
its surrounding walls are also five hundred cubits high.
It is also made of the color of purple-polished gold and is over five hundred li in circumference;
it likewise has seventy-two gates opened.
Within it are eight cities, each more than thirty li in extent;
they are also made of purple-golden color and each has a thousand lanes.
In every alley they face one another, and from every gate they look out upon each other;
there they behold the Dharma King.
Such city walls and enclosures as these are entirely filled with men and women.
Upon hearing this, Śūra was filled with immeasurable joy and leaped for gladness,
exclaiming, "Excellent, excellent!
My great vow is about to bear fruit."
Śūra addressed the fourfold assembly, saying:
"The Great Jewel is about to arrive; do not regard it as something ordinary.
Resolve to cultivate goodness and do not harbor any doubt."
Since I have seen the Great Seer, I have investigated his news thoroughly and have no doubts.
Simply follow my intention: cultivate goodness, revere the Way, and practice asceticism with diligence;
do not act according to your ordinary inclinations.
Reflect upon it and contemplate it; you will surely reach the state of non-action (*anabhisaṃskāra*).
Śūra asked the Great Sage:
"When experiencing pleasure, is there also the music of the lute?"
The Great Seer replied,
"When Candraprabha appears in the world, there will be many kinds of lutes. Śūra said:
"I pray you, explain its meaning.
The Great Sage replied:
"The lute, dance, flute, and song produce immeasurable and most supreme sounds; their carefree wandering is boundless."
He beats the great Dharma drum and blows the great Dharma thunder, shaking the trichiliocosm.
He plants the seeds of noble rank and manifests the lute-play; he fully expresses the sounds of the thirty-six types of drums.
At that moment, the palace of the Deva-king Śakra shook majestically.
The Bhikṣu Śūra asked the Great Sage,
"Just now, I felt no fear toward those malevolent spirits."
"Is there any greater evil than this minor evil?
The Great Sage replied,
"When Candraprabha appears in the world, a great Māra will certainly arise."
Śūra asked, "When the Great Māra appears, can he be repelled?
The Great Sage replied:
"Who is the one person capable of repelling Māra?
The Great Sage replied:
In the Heaven of the Thirty-three, there was a youth named Hètiān (Heaven-Shining).
Riding a celestial dragon-horse, he came through the air,
grasping a pārijāta bow and lùyuǎn arrows.
Only this person can repel this great māra.
The bhikṣu Śūra asked the Great Sage:
"What means are there to repel it?"
"Only this one person can repel it; others cannot.
The Great Seer replied:
These thirty-six great māras each rode upon dragon-horses and carried forty-two golden staffs;
in their left hands, they grasped vajra-pestles.
Holding a *parigha* axe in his right hand, he rushed here and there, trampling stones until they sank ankle-deep;
he leaped across the eternal steps, crying out only "Kill! with no one able to withstand him.
Śūra asked the Great Seer:
"Aside from this great Māra,
what other calamities are there?"
The Great Sage replied,
"When the moonlight approaches its setting,
there will be a calamity. Śūra asked:
"What further calamity will there be?
The Great Sage replied,
"There shall come a time when the sun is darkened for seven days."
There are immeasurable yakṣas, rākṣasas, piśāca ghosts, kumbhāṇḍa ghosts, and flying rākṣasas who devour human beings;
there are only those who uphold the three refuges and the five precepts and practice the dharma of the fast who [are spared].
Such people as these shall all attain liberation. Śūra asked:
"When the Moonlight appears in the world, it is not that the ancient moon has returned, but rather that it is now appearing for the first time."
Those who respectfully practice and cultivate goodness shall all behold him.
Śūra asked, "Furthermore,
where else can one escape from these manifold calamities?"
The Great Seer replied:
"There is only Yangzhou;
next is Xuanmian."
The cities of Gudu, Jicheng, Liucheng, Puzi, Yanghe,
and Jian— among these, this city is the most excellent.
Three great calamities have all arisen therein.
"The rivers of blood flow and the white bones pile up like mountains;
only in the southeast can one attain the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*).
The Great Sage replied:
Śūra said, "I shall instruct the assembly of monks and the laypeople:
practice dhyāna and recite the sūtras, diligently cultivating the three karmas, and do not act as you usually do."
The Great Sage of Brilliant Wisdom is now within the borders of Han.
Before you have seen him, you must diligently cultivate merit and virtue; do not let your intentions remain as they were before.
You must believe and practice goodness, honoring the virtuous.
When Candraprabha appears in the world, things are evil at first but good later;
this degenerate age is difficult to cross.
Exhort and admonish yourselves well, and do not harbor a different mind such as that of the faithless.
The Great Sage replied,
"I shall speak falsely;
if it be not so, may I become a Vajrapāṇi in a future life."
"Grasping a golden pestle in my hand, I shall crush your body into fine dust like motes of powder.
If these words of mine are false,
then in a future life, your body, O sentient being, shall likewise become thus."
Śūra asked the Great Seer,
"Is there currently in this world any seer, noble one,
or sage? The Great Seer replied:
The noble sages and seers in the world are immeasurable.
Śūra asked: "Who are they?"
The Great Seer replied,
"Worthy one, in ancient times the moon was full;
it is for this reason that you did not see it."
Śūra asked, "Who is the name of this worthy man?
The Great Seer replied:
I shall state their names.
Śūra said: "I only pray that you will speak of them."
The Great Sage said: "Seok Hyeon, Deok Yeom,
Hyeon Myeong, Sun Hyeon, Ki Hwa, Hyeon Deok, U Hyeon, Sae Jeong Hyeon, Dang Gwan Hyeon, and Bo Jo Hyeon—
consider these to be the names and titles of the Eight Worthies."
"You may now go to him;
he is truly your guide, capable of transporting you across birth and death. Śūra said:
"Where is he now?
The Great Sage replied,
"He shall appear in the world now."
"What more is there to ask?
One should simply discipline the mind; when the time comes, one will see it.
Śūra bowed again.
"Are there any other worthy ones besides these eight people?
The Great Seer replied,
"There are indeed others."
"Who are these people? The Great Immortal replied:
"Qin Chaoshi, Pan Daocheng, Lu Huiyuan, Ban Guxing, Fu Nan'yang, Liu Daogui, Wang Yanshou, Zhao Xianzong, Zhang Dao, Ban Gu, Shi An, and Li Luocha."
Just as all worthy gentlemen travel throughout the world,
you now cannot distinguish them with your physical eyes;
yet by hearing my constant teaching, you shall practice equanimity.
For what reason?
Because it is difficult to distinguish between the Great Sages and the various Worthies.
Those who receive my command should appropriately be equal in number to the sixteen Righteous Men, the seventy-two Worthies, and three thousand persons together.
Such a Great Being among humans cannot be identified;
some may even see him as insane.
Or again, they may be foolish;
or again, they may be dull-witted, cold, poor, lowly, or base;
or they may drink alcohol and eat meat.
Or again, they may eat at night and thus break their fast;
how can one recognize such manifestations?
They manifest birth with the three poisons and views that follow worldly dharmas, making them difficult to comprehend.
Only through equanimity can one encounter the worthy and holy ones.
The Bhikṣu Śūra addressed the fourfold assembly—bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās:
"A great calamity is about to arrive; do not maintain your usual complacency."
Should there be one's own teachers, parents, sovereigns, donors, friends, acquaintances, relatives,
or kinsmen who obtain this sutra of mine, show it to them all;
do not inquire whether they are near or far— whosoever obtains this sutra of mine.
Exert yourselves in its dissemination so that all may hear it.
Those who do not permit my sutra to be hidden shall inevitably fall into the evil realms in future ages.
The bhikṣu Śūra said: "Suppose there were a person who renounced a trichiliocosm—
including its elephants, horses, the seven treasures, as well as the people within the realm, grain, silk, and wealth— and used them for the purpose of giving."
"It is not as good as someone circulating my sutra;
the merit before all the bhikṣus will be increased a hundredfold. Śūra said:
If anyone obtains my sutra,
they should diligently propagate it throughout cities, towns, and villages, ensuring that men and women, both great and small, all hear it.
As for those who conceal my sutra—
"It is inauspicious in this life and will lead to illness in the future.
Śūra said, "The wise believe it; the foolish reject it."
Śūra said, "My scriptures shall all be fulfilled in the future.
Do not harbor disbelief."
All sentient beings should appropriately practice, follow, rejoice in, and have faith in this sutra;
it is like the ocean, possessing abundant moisture.
At that time, there were more than three thousand people, including the noble lord, the king, ministers, prime ministers, and all officials.
Each heard that there were five hundred immortals atop Taiping Temple, who were leaping for joy;
they each prepared their carriages and went to the location of the immortals within Taiping Temple,
where they bowed their heads in prostration and asked:
"Great Seer, from where have you come and where do you intend to go?
I pray that you will explain your purpose.
The Great Seer replied:
"I have heard that the youth Candraprabha has appeared in the world;
therefore, I have come, desiring to go to that place.
When the king and his ministers heard these words, they [were moved].
They leaped for joy with such rapture that they could not restrain themselves as they turned their hearts toward the west.
"What merits did the True Persons of the Western Land cultivate to encounter and enter the Good?
What wholesome karma did they perform to behold the appearance of Candraprabha in the world?"
"But the people of my country see it from afar and do not see it clearly.
The Great Seer replied,
"When the moonlight appears, all people see it everywhere."
"O King, why do you now give rise to a heart of lamentation?
Upon hearing this, the King, along with Pujin, the great ministers, and all the people, were filled with joy.
Each prepared their magnificent carriages, saying, "We shall now go and return."
The king asked the great seer,
"Where is the youth Candraprabha now?
The great seer replied:
"Excellent, excellent! Great King, listen well to my words.
King Candraprabha is now with a great assembly of three thousand at Mount Penglai, beneath Mount Haoling, in the Grotto of Minzi."
When the time for the cessation of thought arrived,
the great ministers, prime ministers, and all officials of the state of the Noble People, together with the people within the realm,
each addressed the Great Seer, saying:
"Have you followed the Great Sage to the place of Candraprabha and heard [his teaching]?
The Great Sage replied,
"King Candraprabha is like the great ocean and also like the great earth."
They never gave rise to doubt or created obstacles.
The king, the great ministers, and the common people followed the Great Seer;
numbering fifty-seven thousand, they traveled more than seven thousand li from the Land of the Gentleman.
He arrived at the site of Mǐnzǐ’s Cave beneath Mount Hǎilíng on Mount Pénglái.
There he beheld the youth Candraprabha,
with three thousand disciples and various worthies and sages all assembled at that place.
The youth Candraprabha asked:
"O great seers and Great King, from where have you come now, and where do you intend to go?
This place is treacherous and difficult, with no one traveling upon it."
"How have you been able to come here?
The king replied,
"I heard that the World-Honored One was now about to appear in the world, and so I have come to pay my respects and inquire."
The youth Candraprabha said:
"You should simply cultivate goodness and practice with diligent perseverance; do not think as you have done before.
I have now finished."
"Why need there be further inquiry?
The Great King said,
"I have heard that when a holy sovereign appears in the world, I do not know what his laws and principles are."
"Please explain its meaning;
I shall apply my mind to cultivate virtue.
The youth Candraprabha said:
"If you do not know it, I shall explain it for you.
Candraprabha said,
"Listen well, and furthermore, reflect upon it well and contemplate it thoroughly."
Keep this within your heart and do not treat it as an ordinary matter;
I have seen it stated that in years to come there will certainly be a flood disaster.
It rises more than forty *li* above the level plain.
When the waters come, they emerge from its northwest corner and flow toward the southeast.
The great flood’s surging waves and roaring sounds are like thunder and lightning; no metaphor can adequately describe them.
You shall again surge forth, raising a roar like a surging wave.
At that time, all people will be struck with terror, and many will perish from their distress;
only those who maintain pure precepts and diligently seek liberation from the world shall remain.
The youth Candraprabha sent the great dragon king Mahānagna to ferry people across Mount Fu.
Furthermore, suppose there were someone who produced a single scroll of the Avalokiteśvara Sūtra;
or suppose there were someone else who practiced meditative concentration with a single-minded focus.
Furthermore, suppose there is someone who, in this evil age, diligently practices exhortation and conversion;
or suppose there is someone who circulates this sutra so that its chapters, verses, and words are not hidden, diligently practicing exhortation and encouragement.
Such persons as these shall all attain deliverance from the world;
they shall not meet with untimely death by drowning in the calamity of water,
except for those who lack sincere resolve or whose lifespan has come to its end.
Candraprabha further addressed the Great King, saying:
"In the future, when the three calamities prevail and diseases circulate, ten will be wounded and nine will perish;
through various extraordinary afflictions, all shall meet an untimely end."
Your Majesty should believe this.
Issue a decree throughout the kingdom that all those over one year of age who are capable of understanding and speech should receive the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts.
Whether old or young, you must exhort everyone to fully receive the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts and practice the wholesome Dharma.
Such people as these shall all attain transcendence of the world,
except for those who are unwholesome, those who lack sincerity, and those whose life-span has expired.
I now impart this secret teaching to you so that you may know it.
When the Dharma of goodness spreads in an evil age, it will subsequently lead to premature death;
do not harbor regrets. I tell you all:
the world is about to reach its end, and as evil gradually arises, the coming years will be difficult to pass.
To cultivate goodness rather than following ordinary intentions is best.
Even when the world is in calamity, it is not good to follow ordinary intentions;
one should instead strive with diligence to practice the wholesome Dharma rather than following ordinary intentions.
When demons and malevolent spirits are obscure and heroes arise in competition, all things will naturally wear away and perish, and in the end you shall not see me appear in the world.
It is well that you have received my teaching; do not regard it with an ordinary mind.
If one recites the name of Avalokiteśvara one thousand times,
it will protect the person from worldly dangers and bring about the excellent fruit of capture [of demons].
Furthermore, there are those who each receive the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts.
Now you should practice this; do not act according to your ordinary inclinations.
Diligently practice this sutra so that both the old and the young may hear it and attain deliverance from this evil world.
Furthermore, if there should be someone who disseminates this sutra,
causing it to circulate everywhere so that people may hear and know it, thereby attaining deliverance of body and life;
because of such diligent dissemination of this sutra—
They shall also attain transcendence of the world.
Candraprabha said:
"As for those who propagate this sutra..."
Even if I were to calculate this person’s karmic reward for a thousand kalpas,
I could never exhaust it.
Furthermore, should there be anyone who gives rise to doubt and does not believe, [they shall suffer the consequences].
Even if I were to calculate the retribution for this person’s sins throughout a thousand kalpas,
I could never reach the end;
furthermore, I have concealed the words and phrases of one entire fascicle so that no one may hear them.
Because they have covered the eye of wisdom in others, they remain perpetually blind throughout successive lifetimes, seeing nothing at all.
Even upon reaching the stage of Arhat, they are never free from blindness.
Because they obscured the eye of wisdom, they severed the dharmas that remove obstructions and thus incurred this calamity.
Those who receive my command— whether they be inhabitants of cities and villages, kings, ministers, or common people— all shall hear it.
Should there be those with faith who revere this sutra,
you must go to them, regardless of distance, to circulate it and cause them to hear it.
"Let the people of the thousand cities and hundred states all hear this:
I shall appear in the world from north of the Yellow River to south of the Weak Water;
therein, I shall reign as king over the realm of Han."
The Great King addressed the Moonlight King, saying,
"From whence does this sutra emerge?
The Moonlight King replied to the Great King, saying:
More than three thousand people from Hailing participated in the deliberations on what was to be created.
Moonlight addressed the Great King, saying:
"Let the great assembly each disperse separately to transform the world according to its needs; there is no need to return."
At that time, the Great King accepted the instruction, practiced it with joy, and departed.
The youth Candraprabha said,
"If you do not believe what was just spoken,"
Just look at the stone image of Kāśyapa;
it is my record of my appearance in the world.
How excellent that you have joined the severed threads to form a continuous strand!
Thereupon, there were virtuous sentient beings who followed [the teaching] without fear or alarm.
When I emerge into the world, they shall all attain the unconditioned (*asamskrta*).
The King and the great assembly rejoiced and practiced accordingly, remaining close to transformation without indolence.
"I tell you all:
this year has arrived;
you should apply yourselves with diligence and not act as you have been accustomed."
Each made a vow to transcend this evil age.
The Great Seer, the king, along with his ministers and subjects, joyfully practiced [the teaching], paid their respects, and departed.
The five hundred seers remained on Mount Taining.
I also saw the *Moonlight Youth Sūtra* in one fascicle.
Within the City of the Golden Dragon, I beheld a bodhisattva beneath a dragon-flower tree,
seeing a practitioner descend with this sūtra at that time.
"To bring about the mind of all sentient beings for the sake of a single sentient being.
The King said,
"I shall explain this to you in detail."
The Dharma King desires to await the descent of the Sage Ruler;
for the sake of all boys and girls, he maintains one hundred and twenty virtuous rulers.
In the years of Shen and You, he shall preach the Dharma for sentient beings, bringing these boys and girls to the realization of the Way.
When reading this sutra, one should carefully contemplate these words: "A man takes no wife; a woman takes [no husband] as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
The youth Candraprabha desires to bring forth noble accomplishment and to manifest the path for all sentient beings.
If one reads this sutra, one may escape this hardship.
When Bodhisattva Candraprabha wishes to descend to preach that by upholding the precepts one may behold an enlightened ruler,
and when one wishes to recite this mantra:
Lions, tigers, wolves, and furthermore evil spirits and the hundred ghosts will naturally depart.

for the sake of all sentient beings, one should hold the Buddha’s True Dharma in high esteem.

Take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, and take refuge in the Sangha throughout the ten directions of the dharma-realm.

World-Honored One, you have observed that sentient beings commit many offenses;

When a wise ruler appears, this sutra will be spread toward him.

holding a golden staff in hand, they strike others without restraint.

for one hundred days, they must apply their minds with the utmost diligence and refrain from folly and greed during the years of the Earth-Horse and Earth-Cock.
The father does not recognize his son;
the mother does not recognize her daughter.
By recollecting these words of the sutra, one may transform the mind.

the first is to refrain from looking with malicious eyes.
When the Buddha preaches the Dharma for sentient beings, they recover their original minds.

Within this, it is seen that the noble person Candraprabha (Moonlight Bodhisattva) alone was able to save ten people;

If the Lord of Darkness seeks to arise and malevolent spirits seek to flourish, one who exerts diligent vigor shall immediately leave this calamity behind.
Those who follow the Way’s principles should preach the Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings;

yet among those who have died, there are many practitioners whose transgressions were not few.

when practitioners die, they will meet with untimely calamities, and many children will die.

This is my disciple.

it is not merely a matter of looking for a handle at the back."
When ten people point their fingers at one another and shout, they depart in agitation;
how meaningful it is that the youth is joyful after the calamity!
Because of desire, when the two hands at the end of the head clasp one another, they depart in profound stillness.

"Good man, it is well that you have used non-evil persons to exhaust desire for great pleasure. Later, even if one does not question women, one will only achieve the Way through single-minded diligence; thus one may escape this peril."
Furthermore, the Buddha possesses great compassion and deeply pities sentient beings; he does not abandon them, nor does his mind turn back in fear.
When sentient beings reach the end of their lives, those with a karmic connection encounter me, while those without such a connection depart in vain on their own.
Vimalakīrti was together with Dīpaṃkara among human beings;
Vimalakīrti appeared as the wife of Śakra among women so that people would not recognize him.
He manifested as a celestial being who descended from the world of the gods to offer incense.
The dimensions of Vimokṣa are forty-five *li* each; it lies directly to the east.
Within Vimokṣa are the children of the three realms; Vimokṣa delivers people without limit.

When the time for Vimalakīrti’s arrival drew near, immeasurable sentient beings repented their hidden transgressions.
Vimalakīrti delivers people so that they shall certainly attain Buddhahood.
Though Vimalakīrti may appear to covet wealth or speak with deceptive words, all sentient beings can behold him through diligent and focused application of the mind.

The *Vimalakīrti* discusses various meanings regarding the paths; this bird descended beside the sea. When King Sengqing saw this bird with his seven followers, he immediately burned incense, leaping for joy and not eating for seven days.
If all sentient beings hear my voice, they should apply themselves with diligent effort and mindfulness, never entertaining other thoughts.
They must utterly exhaust their evil desires and seek great bliss; they shall not fail to repay their debts to their ancestors.
The Sūtra on the Bhikṣu Śūra (Śūra-bhikṣu-sūtra)
